It's been a while since I found a really delicious Korean restaurant. The place was satisfactory in terms of taste, ingredients, flavor, and price.

-I had high expectations for this place because I heard it was a Korean restaurant run by the nostalgic Tuto Bene chef. These days, a lot of Korean food is too spicy or instant, but this is a place where I really enjoyed it. There were so many menu items, including Korean beef bulgogi, grilled pork belly with red pepper paste, dumpling soup, cold noodles, and soup, that I was worried that the taste would be diluted, but I was unfounded. I especially loved the slightly crispy texture of the Korean beef crispy bulgogi, the less sweet sauce, and the light spicy flavor of the red pepper paste pork belly. As this restaurant specializes in dumpling soup, I am very satisfied with the texture of the dumplings and the depth of the broth. Lamb salad is a taste that seems to divide people's opinions, but if you like lamb, you'll be satisfied.

-It's nice that corkage is available and they have a good selection of soju and beer. However, it is an old-fashioned place that is a bit far from the fancy atmosphere of Tutto Bene in the past.

reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
I wanted to eat onion rings covered in fried breadcrumbs for dinner, so I asked a family member to fry them for me, but they said they didn't want to, so I told them they would go home after dinner, and they said yes.

I ate grilled brisket at home last night, but I remembered the Sinbi Galbisal that YennaPPa had mentioned before, so I decided to stop by.

I had already figured out the location of Sinbi Galbisal while taking a walk, and since it was still early in the evening, there were about two groups of customers, and after receiving guidance from the store entrance, I sat down and ordered a platter of ribs and a bowl of rice.

If someone were to ask what is the most delicious thing, they would probably say that it is high-quality beef grilled over charcoal until the blood just disappears and eaten with salt.

In the past, maybe high-quality pork wasn't as common as it is now, or maybe they just hated the smell of pork. My family didn't eat pork, so the first time I ate pork was when I was serving in the military, and once my unit was in Seoul, I would save money and order bossam from a nearby bossam restaurant, go to the back gate of the unit, pick it up, and eat it in the homeroom. Since I couldn't eat pork, I always only ate the lettuce that came with bossam, and I felt resentful about it. I tasted it, and surprisingly, I started eating it without any smell.

However, I feel like I'm only eating things like pork belly, bossam, or Japanese ramen, so I still can't eat things like stir-fried pork.

When I sat down, my aunt set the table. It consisted of pickled green onions, pickled perilla leaves, kimchi, celery, mayonnaise, garlic, ssamjang, two types of salt, and wasabi, which are the things I like most when eating meat.

I like pickled green onions without any moisture and lightly seasoned with red pepper powder and sugar, and when I tasted it, it felt that way. It doesn't have a higher level of taste like yellow-skinned beef ribs, but it's still good because it's a lightly seasoned type.

I rarely eat pickled perilla leaves, but when I tasted it, it wasn't too salty or too salty.

My aunt brought us a platter of ribs, and a little while later the owner brought us some charcoal.

Looking at the shiny assortment of ribs, the salchi meat already looks good because it has good marbling. This restaurant is not the only restaurant, but there is a mix of some with better marbling and some without.

Put the rib meat on the grill and grill it lightly until the blood just evaporates. Then, I dip it in salt and taste it. It has the unique rich flavor of Korean beef rib meat and the saltiness of the salt. It is a taste that everyone knows, but it is still beef.

Next, I lightly grilled the highly marbled salchi meat, dipped it in salt, and tasted it. It was oily, savory, and juicy, just like the otoro part of tuna. It definitely felt more premium than the rib meat that came with it, so it was good.

I tried adding wasabi to it, but as expected, I like salt, so I only ate it like that once and then only dipped it in salt.

I asked for a refill of the pickled green onions and celery, and I thought 300g would be a bit insufficient, but by the time I finished eating, I was full, so I emptied myself and got up.

While paying, I asked the owner about the raw ribs that can only be tasted with a reservation. He told me that they were bone-in ribs made almost entirely of salchimeat, and that I had to make a reservation a week in advance. The price was 50,000 won per unit.

Overall, I visited this store because it was said to be a store where you can taste 1+, 1++ grade Korean beef rib meat at a relatively low price. It was definitely nice to be able to taste good rib meat at a relatively low price, but I didn't feel that it had much merit compared to the raw ribs from Yellow Sang Beef Galbi, an ultimate rib restaurant.

First of all, stores that sell this type of rib meat are common in Korea and the prices are good, but other than selecting good meat and cutting it well, I don't feel that there is anything special about this store. I don't really feel any special difference from buying good meat from a butcher shop and grilling it at home. If you think that the raw ribs of the yellow beef ribs are the same as the raw ribs that you can only taste at this store by making a reservation a week in advance, of course it will be of higher quality, but the price difference is also big, and more than anything, the vibe of the store and the overall feel are different. The side dishes are better and the taste is better, so I would stop by if I really want to eat Korean beef ribs, but for me, the raw beef ribs of the yellow-sang beef ribs are so good that I don't really notice that they are imported. It is a cut that requires more special effort, but I like it more because it has a soft texture.

Still, it's true that you can taste good Korean beef ribs relatively cheaply, and it's delicious.

The staff grilled the courses themselves at the right timing, so it was good for the two of us to focus on our conversation, and the meat tasted richer thanks to that.

I started lightly with the yuk sashimi and tasted various parts in order, including beef tongue, swallowtail, sirloin, fantail, salchisal, and upjinsal, and it really melted in my mouth.
The steamed oxtail was more memorable because it had a warm and hearty feel thanks to its rich umami flavor. The combination of kimchi stew and pot rice with the subtle scent of charcoal fire finished off the anniversary dinner neatly and heartily.

reviews.author: Namaste
reviews.text:
🌿
Apgujeong is a fine dining restaurant that reinterprets traditional Korean food in a modern way. By experiencing this summer’s limited course ‘Boyang Summer Malkimchalim’, I was able to fully feel the sincerity and aesthetics that went into each dish. The combination of food, plating, taste, sense of space, and service were all excellent.

🍽️Course composition and viewing
1. One bite & ‘taste’ (jeonbyeong, kimchi, yam, sweet potato, spearfish)
• Miniature Korean food that awakens all five senses. Each bite has its own unique flavor, and the contrast of texture and temperature comes together like art. I was especially impressed by the combination of the crispiness of the pancakes and the sweetness of the sweet potatoes.
2. Abalone
• The texture that melts softly in your mouth and the flavor of the fragrant herb oil on the mashed potatoes are truly luxurious. The texture and cooking quality of the abalone were excellent.
3. Yakkong noodles
• The noodles rising like skeins on top of the cold and savory yak bean base create a visual surprise. It's refreshing and light, and it really brings out your taste buds in the summer.
4. Fish soup
• Crispy grilled fish topped with fruits and vegetables for a light yet refreshing taste. The combination of lightness and acidity raised the tension during the meal.
5. Corn per second
• The pancakes, which were golden on the outside and moist on the inside, were topped with corn, grapes, and perilla leaves, making them feel healthy and refreshing at the same time. The seasoning is not excessive, so the original taste of the ingredients remains.
6. Braised beef ribs
• The soft, well-cooked ribs and the black sesame base created a perfect harmony. The garnish wasn't overpowering and it was a flavor worthy of being the pinnacle of a meal.
7. Whole soup & side dishes
• Lastly, the warm rice soup comforts the stomach. The seasoning was just right, and the soup base was deep and rich, which impressed me.
8. Perilla oil ice cream
• The final dessert was a unique ice cream with a subtle hint of fragrant perilla oil, giving it a clean and luxurious finish.

⸻

💡 One-line summary of overall review:
Apgujeong Jakjeok, a traditional Korean food transformed into art – it was a perfect experience that made me remember the seasons through taste. This is a place I definitely want to visit again.

⭐ Rating: 5.0 / 5.0

Also, after cutting the meat into bite-size pieces, they grilled water parsley, kimchi, and green onion kimchi. The kimchi was so delicious, and the sauce that came with the side dish went well with the meat, so I was able to keep eating it without getting tired of it!
​

reviews.author: king
reviews.text: This is Kim Sook-seong, a pork restaurant at Sinsa Station. As the name suggests, you can eat well-aged pork and beef. In particular, the pork was really soft and chewy, and I loved that it was grilled so well. I really liked the various side dishes that helped make the meat even more delicious.

An octopus restaurant where you can feel the hospitality of Gangnam.
